budget_items.topic: Master plan steering committee consultant work
budget_items.what_was_said: The chair said that had Kim Duffy not taken over managing the master plan steering committee's work after it had gone unmet for almost a year, the process would have been a waste of the town's money. He cited the cost as a figure in the captions.

budget_items.topic: 2004 town meeting Ritter addition project (May town meeting project)
budget_items.what_was_said: The chair described a prior, larger proposed addition to the Ritter building that the design committee has now decided not to pursue, in favor of modifying the existing 1963 addition instead.
The design committee is adopting GSA space guidelines to size staff offices in a consolidated Ritter building, with different footage for managers versus staff.

The master plan will include an analysis of the town's excluded debt, showing it is declining as older capital projects from 2004 are paid down, which the chair argued creates capacity to take on new debt for facility needs.
The chair noted a prior town meeting vote directed the town to sell or lease the Brooks House, that this has not been acted on, and that he intends to raise it with the Select Board.

decisions.decision: Vote on approval of the October and November meeting minutes will be deferred to the January meeting since not all members had reviewed the November minutes.
Confirmed the next APDC meeting is January 8, correcting an earlier stated date of January 18.
Nathan will draft and send a letter to the owner of the 50 Main Street office condo over the holidays, a task carried over from the November meeting.
The chair will bring the Brooks House issue back up at the January APDC meeting regardless of the Select Board outcome.

minutes.headline: APDC voted to press the Select Board to act on town meeting's directive to sell or lease the Brooks House.

The precise dollar cost of any Marshall Park or Ritter building elevator/renovation work was not given.

minutes.summary: The Architectural Preservation District Commission (three members present, no public) received updates on 50 Main Street's office condo, the Lunenburg Municipal Building Design Committee's plan to consolidate town offices in the Ritter building using GSA space standards and an elevator rather than the existing chairlift, and the nearly-finished 10-year master plan covering housing pressure from state law, excluded debt, and priority facility projects (Town Hall, Ritter, Turkey Hill, Marshall Park). The commission voted to have a member raise the long-unaddressed Brooks House sell-or-lease town meeting vote with the Select Board, and deferred approval of prior meeting minutes to January.

votes.motion: That the APDC chair represent the commission before the Select Board to press them to act on town meeting's instruction regarding the Brooks House (sell or lease).

what_happened.line: The commission voted 3-0 to have its chair press the Select Board to finally act on a town meeting vote to sell or lease the Brooks House.
A near-final town facilities master plan recommends consolidating town offices into the Ritter building, replacing the existing chairlift with an elevator.
The chair said the master plan will show the town's excluded debt declining, which he argued creates room to borrow for facility projects at Town Hall, Ritter, Turkey Hill, and Marshall Park.
Approval of the October and November meeting minutes was pushed to January because not all members had reviewed them.
A letter to the owner of the 50 Main Street office condo, first raised in November, is still unsent going into the holidays.

why_it_matters: A town meeting directive to sell or lease the Brooks House has sat unacted on; this vote is a push to get the Select Board to move on a decision residents already made.

The facilities master plan under discussion could shape future borrowing and building projects -- Town Hall, Ritter, Turkey Hill, Marshall Park -- that would eventually come back to voters as debt exclusions or town meeting articles.
None of tonight's items were town meeting or ballot votes; they are groundwork -- a letter, a plan, and a request to another board -- that could turn into one later.
